title: Cartesian edges give coherent-realization homotopy pullback squares
statement:
Use quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and Cartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, let $e:b\to c$ be a $p$-Cartesian edge of $E$, and let $a$ be any vertex of $E$. The strictly commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathfrak C[E](a,b)&\xrightarrow{[e]\circ-}&\mathfrak C[E](a,c)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\mathfrak C[B](p(a),p(b))&\xrightarrow{[p(e)]\circ-}&\mathfrak C[B](p(a),p(c))
\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback square of simplicial sets. The vertical maps are induced by $\mathfrak C[p]$ and the horizontal maps are enriched composition by the displayed edge morphisms. A homotopy pullback here means that after a functorial Kan replacement of the diagram, the canonical comparison from the upper left corner to the path-space homotopy fiber product of the other three corners is a weak homotopy equivalence. The four unreplaced enriched mapping sets are not assumed Kan.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (printed pp. 131-132, PDF indices 148-149), via the composition-compatible comparison of Theorem 2.2.5.1; the Cartesian mapping calculation in Proposition 3.2.2.10 (printed p. 184, PDF index 201). Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT copy WANTED.

from.place: Auxiliary categorical comparison: after the coherent-realization mapping-space comparison, a Cartesian edge induces a weak equivalence on enriched mapping simplicial sets by the Cartesian mapping criterion and the contractibility of the standard-simplex mapping posets.
